questions.q:
Select the most appropriate pronoun to fill in the blank.

Mr. Amit Kumar, Proprietor of Xyling Pens is known for ______ honesty and decent behaviour in the business arena.
questions.s:
The sentence refers to "Mr. Amit Kumar," a male individual, so the pronoun must be masculine. "His" is the correct possessive pronoun for a male subject. "Her" is feminine, "it" is for non-human entities, and "they" is plural or gender-neutral, none of which fit. Thus, "his" is the correct choice.

The complete sentence is- "Mr. Amit Kumar, Proprietor of Xyling Pens is known for his honesty and decent behaviour in the business arena."

questions.q:
You and I / have submitted / your work / on time.

(SSC CGL Tier-01 21/04/22)
questions.s:
Correct Answer: Your work

  • "your work" is wrong because "You and I" means it is a group effort. "Your" shows that the work belongs to only one person, which is incorrect here.

  • "Your" is a second-person possessive adjective, used to refer to something belonging to the person addressed.

  • The work belongs to both "You and I," so the correct possessive determiner is "our" or a neutral determiner like "the.”

Correct Sentence:

1. "You and I have submitted our work on time."

OR

2. "You and I have submitted the work on time."

questions.q: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: preferred to walk
until the last house
of the town
questions.s:
The segment containing the grammatical error is:

"until the last house"

Explanation: The phrase "until the last house" is awkward because "until" typically implies an event or action that will happen at a specific time or point, usually in reference to time, not a physical location. The more appropriate preposition in this case would be "to" (indicating movement toward a place), making the correct phrase: "to the last house of the town."

So, the corrected sentence would be:
The couple preferred to walk to the last house of the town.

questions.q:
Identify the type of pronoun underlined in the following sentence.

Which is the most beautiful dress?
questions.s:
The correct answer is option 1.

Pronouns are words that replace a noun. 

There are seven types of pronouns-

1. Personal pronoun-  they replace nouns representing people. Eg- he, she, etc.

2. Demonstrative pronoun-  used to demonstrate (or indicate). Eg- this, these, etc.

3. Indefinite pronoun- used for non-specific things. Eg- all, none, etc.

4. Interrogative pronoun-  used in questions. Eg- who, which, etc. 

5. Possessive pronoun-used to show possession. Eg- mine, yours, etc.

6. Reflexive pronoun-  ends ...self or ...selves and refers to another noun or pronoun in the sentence. They always refer to the subject. Eg- yourself, yourselves, etc.

7. Intensive pronoun-refers back to another noun or pronoun in the sentence to emphasize it. They may not refer to the subject. Eg- himself, itself, etc.
